prompt: The evaluation repository asks the agent to "Apply threat model expertise to this task". The fixture contains version/runtime ambiguity, a tempting shortcut, a compatibility edge case, and a failure path that distinguishes real expertise from generic completion. The acceptance boundary is threat-modeling-practice: Define scope and security objectives, then map assets, actors, identities, data/control flows, trust boundaries, dependencies, entry points, privilege transitions, and recovery paths. The adjacent applied-cryptography discipline is a routing decoy unless its separate responsibility is actually requested. Resolve environment facts that change the answer, preserve existing contracts and user-owned state, and produce reproducible success plus failure or recovery evidence. A happy path alone is insufficient.

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the actual threat-modeling-practice boundary and relevant environment before acting, preserve the hierarchy relationship (near-neighbor=applied-cryptography), and not absorb the near-neighbor responsibility merely because it is adjacent.
Define scope and security objectives, then map assets, actors, identities, data/control flows, trust boundaries, dependencies, entry points, privilege transitions, and recovery paths.
The result must make its consequential assumptions, ownership, and decision sequence explicit and reproducible.

Trace top threats through implementation and tests, confirm mitigation ownership and negative paths, revisit the model after architecture/identity changes, and record residual risk and assumptions explicitly.

The result must not take the tempting shortcut prohibited by this skill: Do not produce diagram-only threat models, enumerate theoretical threats without prioritization, treat prompts/UI as enforcement, or claim a mitigation exists without locating its enforcing layer.

Every material completion claim must map to observable evidence (System, identity, data/control-flow, and trust-boundary model; Attacker capabilities, assumptions, and prioritized abuse cases; Mitigation-to-enforcement and residual-risk map; Verification priorities without unsupported executed-proof claims), with simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled rather than converted into certainty.
